slides.title: What are Neural Networks?
content: AI models inspired by the human brain.
slides.narration:
Have you heard of AI doing amazing things?
Many of these are powered by Neural Networks.
They are AI models.
They are inspired by the human brain.
Neural networks learn from data.
They find complex patterns.
slides.image_prompt: Futuristic graphic illustrating an abstract network of interconnected nodes, resembling a brain.

slides.title: Inspired by the Brain
content: Human brain has billions of neurons.
slides.narration:
So, what inspires them?
Our own brains.
Our brains have billions of neurons.
These neurons communicate.
They process information.
Artificial Neural Networks mimic this structure.
slides.image_prompt: Stylized illustration of a human brain with glowing neural pathways, highlighting connections.

slides.title: The Artificial Neuron
content: Basic unit of a neural network.
slides.narration:
The basic building block is the artificial neuron.
Think of it as a tiny processing unit.
It takes inputs.
It performs calculations.
Then, it produces an output.
slides.image_prompt: Simple diagram of a single artificial neuron with multiple input lines, a central processing circle, and a single output line.

slides.title: Neuron Analogy
content: If signals are strong enough, it turns 'on'.
slides.narration:
Think of a neuron like a light switch.
It gets many electrical signals.
If these signals are strong enough, the switch turns 'on'.
It sends its own signal forward.
Otherwise, it stays 'off'.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a light switch receiving multiple input wires and sending one output wire, with a lightbulb icon turning on/off.

slides.title: Layers in a Network
slides.narration:
Neurons do not work alone.
They are organized into layers.
There are typically three types of layers.
The first is the Input Layer.
It receives the raw data.
slides.image_prompt: Simple diagram showing three distinct vertical layers of circles (neurons): Input, Hidden, Output. Arrows connect neurons between layers flowing left to right.

slides.title: Hidden and Output Layers
slides.narration:
Next come the Hidden Layers.
These layers perform complex computations.
They extract features from the data.
Finally, there is the Output Layer.
It gives the final result or prediction.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram focusing on the connections between hidden layers and the output layer, with data flowing from left to right.

slides.title: How Neural Networks Learn
slides.narration:
How do these networks learn?
They learn by adjusting connections.
These connections are called weights.
It's like tuning a radio.
The network makes a guess.
It compares its guess to the correct answer.
Then, it adjusts its weights to reduce errors.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a neural network with small arrows indicating weights being adjusted. A feedback loop icon showing 'error' being fed back.

slides.title: Learning Analogy
content: Like a child learning to identify objects.
slides.narration:
Think of a child learning to identify animals.
First, they might guess 'dog' for a cat.
An adult corrects them.
The child adjusts their understanding.
Neural networks learn in a similar way.
slides.image_prompt: Child pointing at a cat and saying 'dog', adult gently correcting, child then points at cat and says 'cat' with a happy expression.

slides.title: Where are they Used?
slides.narration:
Neural networks are everywhere.
They power image recognition.
This includes facial recognition.
They are used in natural language processing.
Think of chatbots and translation.
They help in medical diagnosis.
And they create recommendation systems.
slides.image_prompt: Montage of icons representing common AI applications: a camera for image recognition, a speech bubble for NLP, a medical cross for diagnosis, a shopping cart for recommendations.

slides.title: Summary
content: Neural Networks mimic the brain's structure.
They have neurons organized in layers.
Neural networks power many AI applications.
slides.narration:
We learned about Neural Networks.
They mimic the brain's structure.
They have neurons organized in layers.
They learn by adjusting connections.
Neural networks power many AI applications.
slides.image_prompt: A stylized brain graphic connected to a network, symbolizing the summary of neural networks.

content: Think of another real-world application of neural networks.
slides.narration:
Now, here is a small assignment for you.
Think of another real-world application of neural networks.
Describe how it might work.
Discuss it with your peers.
